preamble: Deaffrication of the alveolar ejective affricate: [tsʼ] is realized as the ejective fricative [sʼ]. In Hausa the consonant written ts is transcribed /tsʼ/ by Schuh & Yalwa (1993: 79), who say it "ranges from an ejective alveolar affricate with clear plosive component to an ejective fricative [s']" and that the Kano dialect tends to use the affricate. Newman (2014: 15) describes it as "ejective [s’] or [ts’] depending on dialect", and Wikipedia's ejective article calls [sʼ] a dialectal form of the standard affricate. The sources disagree on details: Wiktionary transcribes Kano Hausa with [sʼ], against Schuh & Yalwa. No source gives a historical direction, so this is recorded as synchronic variation.

languageExamples.context: Ranges from [tsʼ] to [sʼ] by dialect and speaker; Kano tends to the affricate (Schuh & Yalwa 1993: 79)

examples.note: Wiktionary, which labels this transcription Kano; Schuh & Yalwa (1993: 79) say Kano tends to the affricate instead.

sources: Schuh, R. G. & Yalwa, L. D. (1993). Hausa. Journal of the International Phonetic Association 23(2), 77–82. https://doi.org/10.1017/S0025100300004886

Newman, P. (2014). The Range and Beauty of Internal Reconstruction: Probing Hausa Linguistic History. Studies in African Languages and Cultures 48, 13–32. https://salc.uw.edu.pl/index.php/SALC/article/view/99
Ladefoged, P. (2006). A Course in Phonetics (5th ed.), chapter 6 web recordings: Hausa ejectives and laryngealized consonants. Thomson Wadsworth.

related.label: Western Hausa: ts > c' before front vowels
